claims.text: Adding Si to CrFeCoNi enables a high-temperature oxidation transformation not enabled by Mn or Al.
The Si-containing alloy forms a continuous silica-rich oxide layer.
The silica-rich oxide preferentially forms at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
Si facilitates formation of a slow-growing and coherent silica-rich oxide.
The silica-rich oxide has lower intrinsic growth stresses than the oxides formed by the Mn- or Al-containing alloys.
The silica-rich oxide adheres more strongly to the underlying alloy than the comparison oxides.
Reduced oxide growth stress and improved adhesion minimize cracking and spallation above 900 °C.
Mn- and Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form oxide films of compositions different from the silica-rich film.
Oxides promoted by Mn or Al develop higher growth stresses.
The higher growth stresses in Mn- or Al-associated oxides lead to cracking and spallation.
Under identical high-temperature oxidative conditions, CrFeCoNiSi will retain a slow-growing, continuous, adherent oxide layer.
Under those conditions, CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiAl will form less coherent oxides that crack or spall.
CrFeCoNi or CrFeCoNiX with X equal to Mn or Al can serve as baseline comparisons for isolating the effect of Si.
The proposed comparison requires similar processing histories and microstructures for the Si-, Mn-, and Al-containing samples.
The hypothesis is scoped to controlled oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C.
Significant changes in composition, phase separation, or environmental aggressiveness may change the oxidation outcome.
